title: Samuel L. Jackson Says Nick Fury Will Return in 'Avengers: Secret Wars'
summary:
Marvel fans have been wondering about one missing hero. The upcoming movie "Avengers: Doomsday" has a huge cast. Chris Evans is returning as Captain America, Chris Hemsworth is returning as Thor, and many actors from the X-Men movies are joining them to battle the villain Dr. Doom, played by Robert Downey Jr. But one familiar face won't be there: Samuel L. Jackson as Nick Fury.

Nick Fury is the super-agent who first brought the Avengers together as a team. Jackson first appeared as Fury in a short scene after the credits of the 2008 movie "Iron Man." Since then, he has played the character in many Marvel shows and movies.

Now Jackson has confirmed that Fury will be back. In an interview with the website The Direct, Jackson said he won't be in "Doomsday," but he will be in the "movie after this one." That next movie is "Avengers: Secret Wars."

"Secret Wars" is currently scheduled to come out on December 17, 2027. It will be directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, who have directed other Marvel films. Few details about the story have been released. When asked what the movie would be about, Jackson answered, "I have no idea."

The title comes from a big Marvel comic book event published in 1984 and 1985. In that story, a powerful being called the Beyonder whisks dozens of heroes and villains away to a planet called Battleworld. They are told to fight, and the winner gets a wish. In a way, the story is a giant answer to a question many kids have asked: "Who would win in a fight?"

Jackson has other projects coming, too. In 2027, he is set to appear in "The Great Beyond," the next movie from filmmaker J.J. Abrams.
why_it_matters: Big movie series plan their stories years ahead, and fans follow casting news closely. The story also shows how classic comic books still inspire new films.
